review_type: independent AI editorial review of 13 new A2 KNM items (theme 5 history and geography, theme 7 state and law), with every source page opened on 2026-11-22
reviewer: Independent AI reviewer (Sonnet 5.5), separate from the author agent; AI editorial review, not human validation.

meaning_first.independence_note: The blind packet of the author file (hash 557d4b29...d8e) was read first, and the per-item findings were written to content/reviews/110-review.md before the options, keys, notes, plan assignment or any source page was opened. The reviewer then changed prompts, cards and picture briefs; the packet was rebuilt from the proposed bytes (hash b10a246d...3f), the changed items were re-read, and the meaning verdicts below refer to that final packet.

tone_balance.scope_note: All 13 are ordinary civic and history facts; KNM items are never jokes by rule, so they add no light-humor items and the combined program count is unchanged; the coordinator checks it.

edits.before: De Deltawerken zijn grote dammen en sluizen langs de kust. Ze beschermen Nederland tegen hoogwater van de zee. Zo blijft het land droog.
edits.after: De Deltawerken zijn grote dammen langs de kust. Ze houden het water van de zee tegen. Zo blijft het land droog.
edits.reason: Plain words: drop "sluizen" and "hoogwater", say what the dams do.

edits.after: Grote dammen tegen de zee
edits.reason: "Bouwwerken" is above A2; the key now names the dams in plain words.

edits.after: Snelwegen door het hele land

edits.after: Fabrieken die stroom maken

edits.before: Elk jaar is er op 1 juli een nationale herdenking. Wat gebeurde er op 1 juli 1863?
edits.after: Wat gebeurde er op 1 juli 1863?

edits.reason: Explain "afgeschaft" in plain words; drop the weak Grondwet remark.

items.level_reason: Three short sentences, one concrete idea, and no year or place name asked; plainer than most existing theme 3 and 6 KNM cards. The tested term is explained by what the dams do.

evidence.quote: Ze houden het water van de zee tegen
evidence.summary: Rijkswaterstaat, opened 2026-11-22: "Dijken, sluizen, dammen en andere waterkeringen houden water tegen en beschermen ons land zo tegen overstromingen. De bekendste waterkeringen zijn de 13 Deltawerken." Key A (dams against the sea) agrees. B (motorways) and C (power factories) are false statements about the Deltawerken. Key has 5 words, B 5, C 4; the prompt shares no word with the key only. The card stays under 30 words (21).

meaning.situation_summary: A coast scene with a beach, a small red fishing boat and gulls introduces the question what the Deltawerken are; the card then says they are big dams along the coast that hold back the sea.
meaning.communicative_purpose: A newcomer learns what the Deltawerken are, the Dutch flood defence on the coast, a core part of life with water (eindterm 5.1.1).
meaning.contrivance_check: No persona or invented event is needed; the beach picture shows the sea-and-coast setting and no dam, so the key is not visible in the picture or the alt.

items.level_reason: Date-to-event fact with three events of the same kind; the prompt no longer names the commemoration, so the learner must know the date. Terms koloniën, afgeschaft and Grondwet are the subject of the exam theme and are explained on the card.

evidence.quote: Op 1 juli 1863 werd de slavernij in de koloniën van Nederland officieel afgeschaft
evidence.summary: Rijksoverheid FAQ Herdenkingsjaar Slavernijverleden, opened 2026-11-22: "Op 1 juli 1863 werd de slavernij in de voormalige koloniën formeel afgeschaft. Het is ook de datum waarop de Nationale Herdenking Slavernijverleden plaatsvindt." Key C agrees. A: no new Grondwet in 1863 (revisions in 1848 and 1887). B: the first train ran in 1839. The old prompt named the commemoration and so pointed to the only option that fits a commemoration; removed.

meaning.situation_summary: A quiet monument in a park with flowers; the card gives the date, the event and the yearly commemoration in a calm, factual way, without people or detail of suffering.
meaning.communicative_purpose: A newcomer learns the date and the meaning of 1 July 1863 and why Nederland commemorates on 1 July (eindterm 5.1.1, colonies and slavery).
meaning.contrivance_check: The question needs no off-page context: it asks about a date on the card. The three options are three events of the same kind, so none is stocktaking; the picture shows a memorial without naming the event.

items.level_reason: Date-to-event fact; A2 words except the subject terms Holocaust, Joden and slachtoffers. The card defines the Holocaust in one non-graphic sentence.

evidence.quote: Op de laatste zondag van januari herdenkt Nederland de slachtoffers
evidence.summary: Rijksoverheid Nationale herdenkingen, opened 2026-11-22: "Op de laatste zondag in januari is de herdenking van de slachtoffers van de Holocaust in Amsterdam." The same page names the Nationale Holocaust Herdenking "op de laatste zondag in januari". Key B agrees. A: slavery is remembered on 1 July. C: the liberation is celebrated on 5 May. The date narrows the question but both distractors are events with a known other date, so a learner needs the fact, not only the word "herdenkt".

meaning.situation_summary: Candles in jars on a low wall with a tree and a grey winter sky, no people; the card states what the Holocaust was and when the victims are remembered.
meaning.communicative_purpose: A newcomer learns what the Holocaust was and that Nederland remembers its victims on the last Sunday of January (eindterm 5.1.2).
meaning.contrivance_check: No persona is forced in; the date is on the card and in the question. The calm tone follows the plan: no graphic detail, no people in distress, no photographs.

items.level_reason: A direct "why" question whose key follows from the card in plain words; the distractors are two common wrong ideas. Easier than the theme 6 and 8 rule items.

evidence.quote: Mensen uit onder andere Spanje, Turkije en Marokko kwamen werken
evidence.summary: Canon van Nederland (national canon), opened 2026-11-22: "De Nederlandse economie maakt in de jaren zestig overuren en de vraag naar arbeiders groeit enorm. Mensen uit Spanje, Portugal, Griekenland, voormalig Joegoslavië, Turkije en Marokko moeten het tekort aanvullen." The page adds that a recruitment agreement with Turkey followed in 1964. Key A agrees. B (studying) and C (war) are false for the gastarbeiders.

meaning.situation_summary: Hatice asks about her grandfather who came from Turkey in the sixties; the picture shows a man with a suitcase on a platform beside an old train.
meaning.communicative_purpose: A newcomer learns why people from Turkey and Morocco came in the 1960s: Nederland needed workers (eindterm 5.1.2, migration).
meaning.contrivance_check: A family story (the grandfather) is a normal reason to ask about this period; it needs no invented event. The picture shows arrival, not the reason.

items.level_reason: One city out of three, with Amsterdam as the tempting capital answer; same demand as the direct place facts in the bank, with only A2 words.

evidence.quote: De regering zit in Den Haag
evidence.summary: Tweede Kamer audio tour (PDF, 10 May 2023, stop 21), opened 2026-11-22: "Het Binnenhof in Den Haag is een eigenaardige plek. Het is niet de hoofdstad van het land, en toch is hier de regeringszetel gevestigd." The Grondwet states the capital as Amsterdam. Key C agrees; A (Amsterdam) is the capital but not the seat; B (Rotterdam) is neither. Accepted as a responsible-body source because it is the Tweede Kamer itself.

meaning.situation_summary: Sven lives in Amsterdam and asks where the government sits; the picture shows a man walking towards a large building with a flag on an avenue.
meaning.communicative_purpose: A newcomer learns that the capital (Amsterdam) and the seat of government (Den Haag) are different cities (eindterm 5.2.1).
meaning.contrivance_check: Sven living in Amsterdam is exactly the reason to confuse the two cities; no invented event is needed. The picture shows an official building, not the city.

items.level_reason: A number out of three with one plain card; the old second sentence ("bestuur ... staat tussen") was above A2 and is now a size comparison.

evidence.summary: IPO (the provinces' own association), opened 2026-11-22: "In Nederland vormen de provincies de bestuurslaag tussen het Rijk en de gemeenten. Nederland telt twaalf provincies: Groningen Friesland Drenthe Overijssel Flevoland Gelderland Utrecht Noord-Holland Zuid-Holland Zeeland Noord-Brabant Limburg." Key A agrees; eight and sixteen are wrong counts. The key sits in no middle position of a sorted row.

meaning.situation_summary: Priya looks at a map of Nederland and wants to know how many provinces there are; the picture shows her at a table with a plain paper map.
meaning.communicative_purpose: A newcomer learns the number of provinces and that a province lies between a gemeente and the whole country (eindterm 5.2.1).
meaning.contrivance_check: Looking at a map is a normal reason to ask. The map in the picture is deliberately left plain, because a drawn map could show a wrong number of regions and mislead the count.

items.level_reason: A rule fact in plain words; the key is the rule the learner needs for every trip. Distractors are one real misconception (only check in) and one wrong idea (an extra ticket). Comparable to the existing practical KNM rules.

evidence.quote: In het openbaar vervoer checkt u in en uit bij elke reis
evidence.summary: 9292, opened 2026-11-22: "In Nederland werkt het hele OV met een systeem waarbij je moet in- en uitchecken bij elke reis. Je checkt in en uit met een OV-chipkaart of met OVpay." NS says the same for its trains ("Check altijd uit bij de vervoerder waarmee je bent ingecheckt"). Key B agrees. A is false (checking out is required; forgetting it costs money); C is false for a card traveller. The item states only the national rule; no price or fee. The A2 listening item batch105-ov-uitchecken tests a different fact (paying by bank pass in one bus company, with its fee).

meaning.situation_summary: Zeynep travels with her OV-chipkaart and asks what she must do on every trip; the picture shows a woman on a platform with a card in her hand and a train beside her.
meaning.communicative_purpose: A newcomer learns the national OV rule: check in and check out on every trip, with a card or OVpay (eindterm 5.2.2).
meaning.contrivance_check: Using an OV-chipkaart is an ordinary reason to ask about the rule. The picture shows the platform and the card, not the act of tapping, so it does not decide between the options.

items.level_reason: A one-line definition question; the persona no longer describes the answer. Distractors are a pass, a number and a planner, all A2 words.

evidence.quote: 9292 is een reisplanner voor het openbaar vervoer
evidence.summary: 9292, opened 2026-11-22: "Jouw OV reisplanner. Met de 9292 app heb je de reisplanner altijd bij de hand." and "Zie waar de trein, bus, tram of metro is." Key C agrees. A (a bankpas for the bus) is false: 9292 plans journeys and does not pay for them. B (a police number) is false; the alarm number is 112. The source is 9292 itself, which is run by the OV sector; accepted because no government page names the planner and it states what the service is.

meaning.situation_summary: A young woman waits at a bus stop shelter with a bus coming; the card says what 9292 is and what it shows.
meaning.communicative_purpose: A newcomer learns which service plans travel by train, bus, tram and metro in Nederland (eindterm 5.2.2).
meaning.contrivance_check: The prompt asks for the name only; the picture shows a stop and does not show a phone, so neither prompt nor picture gives the key.

items.level_reason: A rule with its condition set up in the prompt ("werk dat evenveel waard is"). Plain A2 wording replaces "werk van gelijke waarde" and "bonussen", so the difficulty is the rule itself.

evidence.summary: Rijksoverheid, opened 2026-11-22: "Alle medewerkers binnen een bedrijf moeten bij gelijkwaardig werk een gelijkwaardige beloning krijgen. Het gaat om alle onderdelen van de beloning. Zoals het salaris, bonussen, toeslagen en secundaire arbeidsvoorwaarden." Key B agrees. A (the boss chooses freely) and C (a man gets more) are false when the work is equally valuable. The prompt no longer shares "gelijk" only with the key. Law on pay transparency is pending; the rule itself is stable, so check yearly.

meaning.situation_summary: Gerrit and Layla do work of the same value in one company; the picture shows a man and a woman side by side at a workbench with a yellow toolbox between them.
meaning.communicative_purpose: A newcomer learns that equal work of equal value must be paid equally, whoever does it (eindterm 7.2.1, equality of women and men at work).
meaning.contrivance_check: Two colleagues at one company is the minimum setting for the rule. The picture shows two workers doing the same task and no pay, so the key is not visible.

items.level_reason: A legal classification question with a stated reason in the prompt. The key was the longest option; it is now a short parallel option. Near batch006-sollicitatie in topic (discrimination in hiring) but another ground and eindterm.

evidence.quote: Dat is discriminatie en dat mag niet
evidence.summary: Rijksoverheid, opened 2026-11-22: "Bijvoorbeeld wanneer een vrouw hoort dat zij geen directeur wordt, omdat zij vrouw is. Direct onderscheid mag niet, behalve als de wet een uitzondering maakt." Key B agrees; the prompt gives the reason (a man is required), so the narrow legal exceptions do not apply. A is false: not a free choice. C is false: no law requires a male director. Options differ in what the law says, not in a literal reading of what the company did.

meaning.situation_summary: Priya applies as a director and the company says a director must be a man; the picture shows a woman and a man across a desk in an office.
meaning.communicative_purpose: A newcomer learns that refusing a woman a job only because she is a woman is discrimination and not allowed (eindterm 7.2.1).
meaning.contrivance_check: A company stating the reason out loud is a blunt but clear example, taken from the government page itself. The picture shows an interview-like scene and the closed folder tells nothing.

items.level_reason: A role question with the stage set in the prompt. "Wetsvoorstel" is now explained on the card; "uitvoeren" and "besproken" are replaced. Comparable to batch007-wetten but about the second chamber.

evidence.quote: Daarna kan de Eerste Kamer het alleen goedkeuren of afkeuren
evidence.summary: Tweede Kamer, opened 2026-11-22: "De Eerste Kamer moet wetsvoorstellen van de Tweede Kamer goedkeuren. Pas als de Eerste Kamer een wetsvoorstel heeft goedgekeurd, mag het wetsvoorstel een wet worden. De Eerste Kamer kan een wet alleen goedkeuren of afkeuren; ze kan het wetsvoorstel niet wijzigen." Key A agrees. B (rewrite) is false: it cannot change. C (choose the regering) is false: the regering is not chosen by the Eerste Kamer.

meaning.situation_summary: A bill goes from the Tweede Kamer to the Eerste Kamer; the picture shows an empty meeting room with benches and a long table.
meaning.communicative_purpose: A newcomer learns how a bill becomes law: the second chamber can only approve or reject (eindterm 7.1.1, two Kamers).
meaning.contrivance_check: The prompt states the stage (from the Tweede Kamer), so the question needs no outside event. The empty room is a setting and shows no vote.

items.level_reason: A meaning question with three clear statements in plain words; "uitvoeren" is replaced by "volgen". Comparable to batch007-europese-unie, which tests another fact (free movement of workers).

evidence.quote: Als lid beslist Nederland mee over de wetten van de EU
evidence.summary: Rijksoverheid, opened 2026-11-22: "Als lidstaat van de EU beslist Nederland mee over wetgeving van de EU." Key B agrees. A (only follow) is false because Nederland takes part in the decisions. C (alone, without the other countries) is false because EU laws are decided with the other member states. The key is the shortest option.

meaning.situation_summary: Jeroen reads that Nederland is a member of the EU and wants to know what that means for EU laws; the picture shows him at a kitchen table with a newspaper and two small flags on the windowsill.
meaning.communicative_purpose: A newcomer learns that membership means Nederland takes part in deciding EU laws (eindterm 7.1.2).
meaning.contrivance_check: Reading the paper is a normal reason to ask. The flags are a setting detail; the card, not the picture, carries the fact.

items.level_reason: A who-decides question with the condition in the prompt ("zij komen er samen niet uit"). Three bodies a learner knows. Plain words except the terms rechter and burgemeester.

evidence.summary: Rechtspraak.nl, opened 2026-11-22: "Als 2 partijen een conflict hebben over de regels, beslist de rechter." Key A agrees. B (politie) is false: the police enforce rules but do not decide who is right. C (burgemeester) is false: the burgemeester does not settle a private dispute between neighbours. Not a repeat of batch007-hoger-beroep, which asks about appeal.

meaning.situation_summary: Milan and his neighbour disagree about a fence and cannot solve it themselves; the picture shows two men on either side of a low fence with their arms crossed.
meaning.communicative_purpose: A newcomer learns that when two sides cannot agree, the rechter decides (eindterm 7.1.3, separation of powers).
meaning.contrivance_check: A fence between neighbours is a typical dispute and the prompt says they could not settle it. The picture shows the dispute and not the decider.
